summary: William L. Smith is an Indology scholar who held a post at Stockholm University (~1980–2007). He also held positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Hampton University, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

William M. Bodiford specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of Kansas, Yale, Komazawa, and Tsukuba under Stanley Weinstein and others, he held posts at Meiji Gakuin, Iowa, and UCLA (~1992).

William M. Gorvine works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Connecticut College (-1991) and an M.A. (-1997) and Ph.D. (-2006) at the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano.

William Magee specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia, where he was a professor (attested 1992), and held posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College and Chung-Hwa Institute.

William R. LaFleur was a Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1969–1973). He held posts at Princeton (~1971–1976), UCLA (~1980–1989), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

William Rainey Harper was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He studied under William Dwight Whitney at Yale University (~1873–1875) and later held posts at Denison University (~1876–1879) and the University of Chicago (~1891–1906).
William Robertson was a historian and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1735–1741) and later held a post there from approximately 1762 to 1793.
William Roxburgh studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1770–1772) and the University of Aberdeen (~1790). In 1793, he directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

William S.-Y. Wang is a linguistics and Sinology scholar who studied at Columbia University (~1951–1955) and the University of Michigan (~1955–1960). He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1966–1995) and Hong Kong Polytechnic University (~2004).
William Stede was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of London from approximately 1928 to 1949.

William Theodore de Bary was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University and Harvard University, later serving as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia from approximately 1953 to 2017.

William Van Gordon is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (both attested 2015).

William Wilson Hunter studied at The Glasgow Academy, Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn. Working in Indology and history, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887) and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1886–1890).
William Woodville Rockhill was a Tibetology and Sinology scholar. He studied at Lycée Condorcet and the École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873).

William Wright was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at the University of St Andrews. He held posts at UCL, the British Museum (~1861–1870), and the University of Cambridge (~1870–1889; Adams Professor 1887).

Willibald Kirfel was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn (~1904–1908). He later served at the University of Bonn as a librarian and Privatdozent in 1920, ultimately succeeding Jacobi.

Wilt L. Idema is a Sinology scholar who studied under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé at Leiden University (~1963–1974). He held posts as professor at Leiden (1975–1999) and at Harvard University (~1999–2013), and was a Radcliffe fellow (2001–2002).
Winfred Robert Martin worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and held a post as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who studied at Cornell (~1968–1971). She held posts at Washington and Lee (~1994–2000), the University of Chicago (~2000–2005), and Indiana University (~2010).
Winston Kyan is a scholar in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Wu Hung (attested 2006).
